newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM KILLS 12,000 PIGS TO KEEP OUT SWINE FEVER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM KILLS 12,000 PIGS TO KEEP OUT SWINE FEVER.

text.p: Belgium will slaughter 12,000 pigs on Monday and Tuesday to prevent highly contagious swine fever from spreading into farms in Belgium from the Netherlands, a Belgian agriculture ministry spokeswoman said.
"This is one of the firmest measures we could possibly have taken," a spokeswoman for Farm Minister Karel Pinxten said.
She said the 12,000 pigs had been imported from the Netherlands since January 15 and were spread over 38 farms in Flanders, the northern half of Belgium.
About 800,000 pigs were slaughtered in Belgium after various outbreaks of swine fever in the early 1990s. "So this is actually peanuts compared with the number of pigs slaughtered then," she said.

Two more cases of the disease, which is not harmful to humans, came to light last weekend in the southern Dutch province of North Brabant, bringing the number of cases discovered in the Netherlands so far to 16.
Last week the European Union's Standing Veterinary Committee backed a ban on exports of pigs from seven Dutch districts.
Last year, the Netherlands exported almost a million tonnes of pigs and pork products, about 60 percent of its production.

Cases of swine fever were first reported in Germany at the start of the year. Belgium banned the import of all live pigs from Germany last month and extended this ban to most parts of the Netherlands last week after cases were also discovered there.
